messages:
Maria Chen: Quick status check for ACME on‑prem activation — want to lock the milestone gating list and who owns the egress fallback if customer can't open outbound 443. Images are green in our build, but cert signing + NAT rules are pending. @Kevin, @Denise, @Arjun, pinging for owners.

Kevin Patel: I've got the CSR in flight, just waiting on the customer's signed SAN list. ETA EOD tomorrow from my side. Who is their network contact?

Denise Raghav: I'll take NAT/firewall verification. Need a sample NAT policy or iptables nat rules from their infra to validate stateful expectations. Also we should plan a fallback to our redwood-proxy egress (limited throughput) if their egress is restricted.

Arjun Sinha: Runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/onprem-activation (internal). ops-bot shows image build/push done, but airgap transfer status is partial: 2/3 hosts synced.

ops-bot: image-sync: host-02 failed checksum, retry scheduled in 5m. log snippet: `scp: transferred 42%`

Lee Morgan: For canary sequencing — propose: start with single control node (no GPU) for config smoke, then 3-node GPU canary after network smoke passes. Keeps blast radius small.

Maria Chen: +1 to Lee. Denise — if NAT takes longer than 48hrs, fallback plan is to route traffic via redwood-proxy; that requires token rotation before activation. Who can do token rotate when needed?

Samir Ortiz: I can handle token rotation and the limited-scope key issuance. Will need a quick security exception for canary window. @security-bot FYI.

Denise Raghav: Kicking off NAT checks today. Sending `traceroute` & `tcpdump` requests to their infra. Please confirm allowed source ranges we can ask them to open — I have 18.65.32.0/24 currently on the contact sheet, is that accurate?

Maria Chen: Confirmed: allowlist should include 18.65.32.0/24 and 18.65.33.0/24 for the canary. I'll DM the customer's network owner and CC you.

Arjun Sinha: Heads up — we saw a cert chain issue in staging where the intermediate CA was missing from their side; that breaks mTLS. If they can't provide the chain, we can short-term allow TLS-only for the initial canary (audit-logged), but need signoff.

Denise Raghav: Agree but need explicit approval for disabling client-auth for canary. Samir — can you start the security review for a timeboxed exception?

Samir Ortiz: I can approve a 24h exception for canary with strict audit logging and ticketed follow-up. I'll attach the exception to ticket ACME-204 and include required compensating controls.

Maria Chen: Great — owners for clarity: certs -> Kevin; NAT/firewall -> Denise; image transfer -> Arjun; token rotation & security exception -> Samir. Milestone: "canary start" target 2026-04-03. If any blocker slips that changes the date, please update thread with a short note. Thx all. :thumbsup:
